title: Demand rises

predict.q: Demand for the good rises (a parallel shift right). Supply does not change. What happens to consumer surplus and producer surplus?

options.fb: The higher price is more than offset by more units and a higher demand curve: CS 80 → 125, PS 160 → 250.

options.s: Consumer surplus falls because price rises; producer surplus rises.
options.fb: Price rose, but the new demand curve is higher and more units are bought: CS = ½ × 50 × (19 − 14) = 125, up from 80.

options.s: Consumer surplus rises; producer surplus falls.
options.fb: Sellers get a higher price on more units: PS must rise.

options.s: Neither changes: surplus just moves from buyers to sellers.
options.fb: Total surplus grows because more mutually beneficial trades happen.

task: Move the demand slider from 16 to 19 and watch the two shaded areas and their values.

target.do: Move the demand intercept slider from 16 to 19, then press Check.

takeaway: A parallel rise in demand raises both surpluses; the higher price is more than offset by more units and a higher demand curve.
